title: Suspension Cell Based AAV Production and Purification
author: Jin Hyung Chung
materials: CRITICAL All reagents used for viral production and administration should be prepared using endotoxin-free materials. Glassware is not endotoxin-free, and autoclaving does not eliminate endotoxins. To minimize contamination, we dissolve chemicals in sterile bottles by shaking and/or heating to mix, use demarcations on bottles to bring solutions to the final volume, and use pH strips rather than a pH meter. When filter-sterilizing solutions, do so in a biosafety cabinet. Grow bacterial stocks in LB or Plasmid+ media containing the appropriate selective antibiotic; refer to the Addgene catalog for suggested growth conditions. Use a large-scale endotoxin-free plasmid purification kit to isolate plasmids; elute plasmid DNA with the supplied Tris-EDTA (TE) buffer. Measure the DNA purity and concentration using a spectrophotometer and freeze at -20 °C or -80 °C for up to several years. CRITICAL Verify the integrity of purified plasmids by Sanger sequencing and restriction enzyme digest, or through whole plasmid sequencing before proceeding with downstream applications. pAAV plasmids contain ITRs (Fig. 6) that are necessary for replication and encapsidation of the viral genome. Because ITRs are prone to recombination in E. coli , pAAVs should be propagated in recombination-deficient strains such as NEB Stable, Stbl3, or SURE 2 competent cells. Presence of ITRs in purified pAAV genomes can be assessed through restriction enzyme digest with SmaI (use sequence-editing and annotation software to determine the expected band sizes). Note that it is difficult to Sanger sequence through the secondary structure of ITRs 68 ; avoid ITRs when designing sequencing primers. Alternatively, whole plasmid sequencing with Oxford Nanopore Technology (e.g. as offered through Plasmidsaurus) is able to fully sequence the ITRs. Create bacterial glycerol stocks and store at -80 °C for up to several years. Fig. 6 | A modular AAV toolbox for cell type–specific gene expression (from Challis et al., Nat Protoc 14 : 379)

! CAUTION AAVs are biohazardous materials and must be handled according to governmental and institutional regulations. Experiments involving AAVs were performed using biosafety level 2 practices as required by the California Institute of Technology and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. CRITICAL The entire procedure spans 3 d, excluding pause points and the time required to evaluate transgene expression (Fig. 7a). Once cells have been transfected, AAVs are harvested on day 3. Plan accordingly during this time window. In the referenced protocol, a Type 70 Ti rotor is used for ultracentrifugation of the AAV through a density gradient (Steps 32-37). This rotor can hold 8 tubes, allowing for simultaneous purification of 8 separate AAV variants, at 1-8 plates (150 mm plates) per variant. To increase throughput, we also provide a smaller scale purification workflow with a Type 70.1 Ti rotor, which can allow for purification of 12 separate AAV variants, at about 1-3 plates (150 mm plates) per variant.

During ultracentrifugation, gather the supplies and equipment for Steps 39-42. Assemble the clamp setup (Equipment setup) and collect one of each of the following per gradient: PES Ultra-15 centrifugal filter device, 5-ml syringe, 10-ml syringe, 0.22-μm syringe filter unit, and a 16-gauge needle.

Prepare the supplies for Steps 41 and 42. First, remove and save the plunger from a 10-ml syringe. Attach a 0.22-μm syringe filter unit to the syringe barrel and place it on top of an PES filter device. Next, add 10 mL of DPBS supplemented with 0.001% of Pluronic F-68 (DPBS + 0.001% Pluornic F-68) to the barrel and allow the solution to begin dripping through the syringe filter unit and into the filter device (Fig. 8f). Last, attach a 16-gauge needle to a 5-ml syringe. CRITICAL STEP ( Optional ) Rinse the filtration membrane of the PES filter device by adding 15 mL of DPBS + 0.001% Pluornic F-68 to the top chamber and centrifuging at 3000 x g, Room temperature, 1 minute ; discard the flow-through. The manufacturer recommends using the device immediately after rinsing.

steps.title: Prepare Reagents and Buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare the necessary buffers and reagents for AAV production and purification.

substeps.instruction: Warm CTS Viral Production Medium (Thermofisher, A5144001) to 37 °C before use.

Prepare SAN digestion buffer: Add 29.22 g NaCl, 4.85 g Tris base, and 2.03 g MgCl2·6H2O to a 1-liter bottle of WFI water; shake to mix, filter-sterilize, and store at room temperature (final pH ~10.0; 500 mM NaCl, 40 mM Tris base, 10 mM MgCl2).
Prepare SAN + SAN digestion buffer on the day of use: Add 100 U of SAN (4 µL of 25 U/µL SAN) per milliliter of SAN digestion buffer and pipette to mix.

Prepare 2.5 M NaCl / 40% (wt/vol) PEG stock: Decant ~500 mL WFI into a sterile bottle. Add 146.1 g NaCl to the remaining 500 mL WFI, shake/heat until dissolved. Add 400 g PEG and heat at 37 °C overnight (up to 2 nights) or at 65 °C until dissolved. Add reserved WFI to reach 1 L total volume. Pre-wet filter surface with water, then filter-sterilize and store at room temperature.

Prepare High Salt Buffer: Add 29.22 g NaCl, 93.2 mg KCl, and 101.7 mg MgCl2·6H2O to a 500-ml bottle of DPBS; shake, filter-sterilize, and store at room temperature (final: 1 M NaCl, 2.5 mM KCl, 1 mM MgCl2).

Prepare Low Salt Buffer: Add 2.92 g NaCl, 93.2 mg KCl, and 101.7 mg MgCl2·6H2O to a 500-ml bottle of DPBS; shake, filter-sterilize, and store at room temperature (final: 100 mM NaCl, 2.5 mM KCl, 1 mM MgCl2).
Thaw TransIT-VirusGen Transfection Reagent and RevIT AAV Enhancer to room temperature and vortex gently.

steps.title: Maintain and Seed HEK293T Cells
steps.instruction: Thaw and maintain AAV-MAX suspension cells according to manufacturer recommendations.

substeps.instruction: Seed cells in 30 mL Viral Production Medium in a vented 125 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Maintain on an orbital shaker in a cell culture incubator at 37 °C, 5-8% CO2, at 125 rpm.

Passage cells every 3-4 days: seed at 6E5 cells/mL for 3-day passaging or 3E5 cells/mL for 4-day passaging. Use flasks with at least 4x the media volume (e.g., 125 mL flask for 30 mL media; 2 L flask for 480 mL media).
Passage cells at a density of 3E6 cells/mL.
Verify cells are at least 95% viable via trypan blue exclusion prior to transfection.

steps.title: Prepare Transfection Complexes
steps.instruction: Form the DNA-reagent complexes for transfection.

substeps.instruction: Combine transgene, AAV capsid, and pHelper plasmid at a ratio of 1:2:0.5 in a sterile tube (total DNA: 2 μg per mL of cell culture). Mix thoroughly.
Add 1 μL of RevIT AAV Enhancer per 1 mL of total suspension cell culture to the DNA and PBS. Mix thoroughly.
Transfer the DNA mixture into 100 μL of PBS per 1 mL of suspension cell culture in a separate sterile tube.
Add 3 μL of TransIT-VirusGEN Reagent to the diluted DNA:RevIT mixture and mix thoroughly via inversion or vortexing. Do not agitate again after this step.
Incubate the mixture at room temperature for 15-45 minutes.

steps.title: Transfect and Culture Cells
steps.instruction: Transfect the cells and incubate for viral production.

substeps.instruction: On the day of transfection, passage cells at 3E6 cells/mL and incubate at 37 °C, 5-8% CO2.
Add TransIT-VirusGEN:RevIT:DNA complexes to the cell culture, swirling gently to distribute.
Incubate flasks on an orbital shaker at 125 rpm, 1.9 cm orbital throw, 37 °C, 5-8% CO2 for 72 hours (or 48 hours if time is limited).

steps.title: Harvest and Clarify Cell Culture
steps.instruction: Collect the cells and media and separate the cell pellet.

substeps.instruction: Collect media and cells using a 50-ml serological pipette into a conical centrifuge tube (e.g., 250 mL tube for 240 mL culture).
Centrifuge at 2000 x g at room temperature for 15 minutes to form a cell pellet.
Pour off the supernatant (clarified media) into a reserved media bottle.
Centrifuge the pellet again at 2000 x g for 1 minute; remove remaining media with a P1000 pipette and add to the reserved supernatant.

steps.title: PEG Precipitation of AAV from Media
steps.instruction: Recover AAV particles from the clarified media using PEG precipitation.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the reserved supernatant into a conical tube.
Add 1/4 volume of 40% (wt/vol) PEG stock solution (final concentration 8% wt/vol).
Invert ten times to mix and incubate on ice for at least 2 hours (or 4 °C overnight).
Centrifuge the mixture at 4000 x g, 4 °C, for 45 minutes to form a PEG pellet.
Pour off the PEG-clarified media into a bleach bottle.
Centrifuge again at 4000 x g, 4 °C, for 5 minutes; remove remaining supernatant with a P1000 pipette.

steps.title: Cell Lysis and Digestion
steps.instruction: Lyse the cells and digest nucleic acids using SAN buffer.

substeps.instruction: Prepare SAN + SAN digestion buffer: 8 mL (for Type 70 Ti rotor) or 4 mL (for Type 70.1 Ti rotor) per 120 mL of harvested cell culture.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 6 mL (Type 70 Ti) or 2.4 mL (Type 70.1 Ti) of SAN + SAN digestion buffer using a 10-ml serological pipette, then finish resuspending in a 50-ml tube.
Incubate in a 37 °C water bath until the purification steps begin (or store at 4 °C overnight).

steps.title: Combine Lysate and PEG Pellet
steps.instruction: Merge the recovered AAV from the media and the cell lysate.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the PEG pellet in 1 mL (Type 70 Ti) or 0.3 mL (Type 70.1 Ti) of SAN + SAN digestion buffer per 120 mL of culture using a P1000 pipette until smooth.
Combine the resuspended PEG pellet with the cell lysate from the digestion step.
Incubate in a 37 °C water bath for an additional 30 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Iodixanol Density Gradient
steps.instruction: Create the density gradient in OptiSeal tubes.

substeps.instruction: Use 32.4 mL OptiSeal tubes (Type 70 Ti) or 8.9 mL OptiSeal tubes (Type 70.1 Ti).
Layer the following iodixanol solutions from bottom to top using a 2-mL serological pipette (or electronic repeater pipette with modified tip):
Bottom layer: 60% iodixanol in low salt buffer with phenol red (3 mL for Type 70 Ti; 0.8 mL for Type 70.1 Ti).
Second layer: 40% iodixanol in low salt buffer (5 mL for Type 70 Ti; 1.5 mL for Type 70.1 Ti).
Third layer: 25% iodixanol in low salt buffer with phenol red (4 mL for Type 70 Ti; 1.2 mL for Type 70.1 Ti).
Top layer: 15% iodixanol in high salt buffer (6 mL for Type 70 Ti; 1.8 mL for Type 70.1 Ti).
Ensure sharp delineations between layers; remove air bubbles by tapping or using a pipette tip.

steps.title: Load Lysate onto Gradient
steps.instruction: Add the digested lysate to the top of the gradient.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the combined lysate (from Step 8) at 2000 x g, room temperature, for 10 minutes.
Slowly load the clarified lysate supernatant onto the 15% iodixanol layer using a 2-ml serological pipette (approx 9 mL for Type 70 Ti; 2.7 mL for Type 70.1 Ti).
After loading 6-7 mL, spin at 3000 x g, room temperature, for 15 minutes, then load the remaining supernatant using a P200 or P1000 pipette.
Fill any remaining space to the neck of the tube with SAN buffer.
Secure with a black cap and spacer.
Balance tubes to within 5-10 mg using lysate or SAN buffer.
Load tubes into the ultracentrifuge rotor and fasten the lid.
Centrifuge at 350,000 x g, 18 °C: 1 hour 30 minutes for Type 70 Ti (58,400 rpm) or 1 hour 15 minutes for Type 70.1 Ti (61,700 rpm).
Use acceleration profile no. 3 and deceleration profile no. 9.

steps.title: Collect Purified AAV
steps.instruction: Extract the AAV from the density gradient.

substeps.instruction: Remove the tube and secure it in a clamp over a beaker of 10% bleach.
Using a needle/syringe, insert the needle ~4 mm below the 40/60% interface.
Collect 3.5-4.0 mL of virus/iodixanol from the 40/60% interface and the 40% layer, avoiding the white protein layer at the 25/40% interface.
Optional: Re-extract AAV from the pellet by adding 3 mL (Type 70 Ti) or 1 mL (Type 70.1 Ti) SAN buffer, vortexing, and centrifuging at 3000 x g for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Buffer Exchange and Concentration
steps.instruction: Remove iodixanol and concentrate the virus using a PES filter device.

substeps.instruction: Add the 3.5-4.0 mL virus/iodixanol to a syringe barrel containing 10 mL DPBS. Layer virus below DPBS and push through a syringe filter into a PES filter device.
Centrifuge at 3000 x g, room temperature, for 5-8 minutes (or until volume in top chamber is 500-1500 µL).
Discard flow-through. Add 13 mL DPBS + 0.001% Pluronic F-68 to the top chamber and mix with a P1000 pipette.
Repeat the centrifugation and wash process for a total of four buffer exchanges.
During the final spin, retain 150-200 µL of solution in the top chamber.

steps.title: Final Recovery and Storage
steps.instruction: Recover the concentrated AAV and store.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the virus from the top chamber to a 1.6-ml screw-cap vial using a P200 pipette.
Wash the PES filter walls 10 times with 150-200 µL of DPBS + 0.001% Pluronic F-68 to recover residual AAV; combine with the virus in the vial.
Optional: Filter-sterilize by transferring to a Costar Spin-X filter unit and centrifuging at 3000 x g for 1 minute.
Store the final product in screw-cap vials at 4 °C.
